title: Random Location Generator: Anywhere on Earth
description: Generate a truly random location anywhere on Earth with the Random Location Generator — equal-area sampling, land-only option, no favourites. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, half of all truly random points fall within 30 degrees of the equator — not by bias, but because half the sphere's surface lies in that band. The ocean takes about seven in ten.
quick_answer: The Random Location Generator picks a point uniformly over the Earth's surface — every square kilometre equally likely — and shows it on the map with its coordinates. Press generate and land somewhere honest: usually ocean, sometimes a place you will now spend ten minutes reading about.

body.t: Daily random-point challenges, 'where in the world' quizzes and classroom lotteries need a generator with no favourite continents. The
explores the neighbourhood of whatever lands.
Some travellers genuinely go. A random land point within reach is a trip-planning seed no algorithm's recommendation engine would dare make.
Monte Carlo work over the sphere needs correct area-uniform points — naive latitude-uniform sampling over-weights the poles, the classic error this generator avoids.
A random real place as a story's anchor — researched afterwards, chosen by nobody. Fiction with receipts.
Oceans cover about 71% of the surface, so roughly seven generates in ten splash. Land-only mode exists because most humans' curiosity is terrestrial — the toggle is labelled, the odds are published.

Picking latitude uniformly at random would crowd points near the poles (where longitude lines converge). Area-uniform sampling thins them correctly — draw many points and the map fills evenly, pole to pole.

faq: Can I get a random point in a specific region?
Constrain by generating and keeping the points that fall in your region, or use the land/country modes the tool offers — rejection sampling keeps the statistics honest inside any boundary.
Why did I get the middle of the Pacific twice?
The Pacific is the largest target on Earth — about a third of the surface is its neighbourhood. Randomness has no memory and no mercy.
Yes — no weighting from your history. Streaks of ocean are the distribution working, not the generator sulking.
Draw a random point within a radius instead — the radius tools on this site frame that job; a sphere-wide generator's 'near me' would be a different instrument.
Can I seed or reproduce a draw?
Note the coordinates — they are the record. The generator's job is fresh randomness, not replay.
A random point plus the reverse geocoder's record tells you what is there — frequently nothing with a name, which is itself the geography lesson.
